newsitem.title: UK: Study confirms porcupines do it...carefully.
newsitem.headline: Study confirms porcupines do it...carefully.

text.p: Careful study has confirmed what common sense would dictate -- when porcupines mate, they do it very, very carefully.
But, according to New Scientist magazine, female porcupines find those quills sexy, if dangerous.

Rick Sweitzer of the University of California at Davis and Joel Berger of the University of Nevada say a porcupine's quills could have evolved as much for sexual display as for protection, the magazine reports.
A five-year study of the animals shows females will mate only with older and larger males, Sweitzer and Berger said.

It could be the females go for males that can win in fights -- which can be vicious. "After a fight the loser can have anywhere between 30 to 50 quills stuck in his face and chest," Sweitzer told New Scientist.
"It must be extremely painful walking around with dozens of someone else's quills stuck in your face."
During mating females rarely got spiked, they added.
